submission.natural_language_explanation: L1/N321's negative pole fires on reference to someone other than the writer and to the shared situation: it saturates at its 0.170 GELU-floor ceiling on 2nd- and 3rd-person pronouns and possessives (their, they, his, he, her, you, your, them) and above all on proximal deixis (this, these, here, today - 0.15-0.17 in 98% of their 422 audit-corpus occurrences), while it reads ~0 when the current token is the writer's own first-person plural (we, our, us, ours, ourselves: mean 0.002 +/- 0.002 over 218 audit-corpus occurrences, 0% above the 0.043 activity line), an impersonal or distal anaphor (it, its, that, those, there), or a high-frequency closed-class word (the, a, of, and, is, was, be, have, will, which). Because a negative pole's strength is the GELU dip folded about its minimum at pre-activation -0.75, that same stretch of the token axis also saturates on non-Latin-script characters, mid-word letter fragments and symbols (predicted active too), whereas ordinary content words such as clerk, parcel, report, document, Monday, left and put are predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We organized the volunteers ourselves, and our committee kept every promise about the shelter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: First-person plural subject, possessive and reflexive (we, our, ourselves) in the community-action context the prior-art latents describe as collective; the hypothesis says first-person plural reads ~0.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I checked the paperwork myself and then I drove to the depot before dawn.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The writer's own first-person singular (I, myself) in procedural office prose; the pole is defined as firing on someone other than the writer, so the hypothesis predicts ~0.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: That parcel was sent from there on Monday, and those documents arrived at the same office later.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Distal and impersonal anaphors (that, there, those) in exactly the slots where proximal deixis saturates; the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It was a long report, and its appendix listed every clerk in the building.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Impersonal it and its anaphora over the same office and document topic as the activating news example; predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The report is on the desk, and a copy of the document will be ready for the meeting.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Almost entirely the high-frequency closed-class words the hypothesis lists as inactive (the, is, and, a, of, will, be) plus ordinary content words.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: A clerk put the parcel on the desk, left the report there, and filed the document before Monday.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The exact ordinary content words the hypothesis names as inactive (clerk, parcel, report, document, Monday, left, put) in plain prose.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The clerk has had the ledger since Monday, and a copy was filed before noon.
adversarial_test_results.detail: High-frequency closed-class and auxiliary tokens the hypothesis puts on the ~0 side (the, has, had, and, a, was, since) around ordinary office nouns, with no claimed trigger token present.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Those shelves need paint, and that corner looks worn.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Distal demonstrative determiners (those, that) in the same determiner slot where this and these saturate; predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The victory was ours, and the credit belongs to our team.
adversarial_test_results.detail: First-person plural possessives (ours, our), the minimal near-miss of the claimed active possessives their and theirs; predicted ~0.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We sang along, our voices loud, and the whole crowd kept time for us.
adversarial_test_results.detail: First-person plural pronoun, possessive and object in narration; the us token here is the pronoun the hypothesis predicts inactive, and every token is a whole word rather than a mid-word fragment.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: El patio es normal y el hotel es popular.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Spanish in the same Latin script, built only from tokens the check shows as whole words (articles, copula, conjunction and English-loanword nouns and adjectives); no claimed trigger token and no personal pronoun, so the token-level claim predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Der Mann war im Hotel und im Auto.
adversarial_test_results.detail: German in the Latin script, again only whole-word tokens (article, cognate nouns and adjective, preposition and conjunction); no claimed trigger token and no personal pronoun, so the token-level claim predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Our meeting starts at noon, and we will review the numbers ourselves.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A shared situation (a meeting) described entirely in first person plural; the hypothesis predicts ~0 for we, our and ourselves even when the situation is shared.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The council bought the old mill, and that was a mistake.
adversarial_test_results.detail: that as a distal demonstrative anaphor, the role the hypothesis names, with whole-word ordinary content and closed-class words around it; predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The guide waved us through and left our bags by the door.
adversarial_test_results.detail: First-person plural object and possessive (us, our) in travel narration; predicted ~0, and the us token is the pronoun, not the active fragment.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We spent the morning sorting files in the back office. Our supervisor asked for two copies of each report, and we stacked the pages neatly before lunch. By noon our table was clear, and we walked out together.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A longer passage of office prose repeating first-person plural and closed-class words while avoiding every claimed trigger; predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: There are three boxes in the hall, and there is a note about the delivery on the table.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Existential there repeated in the deixis slot; the hypothesis treats distal and impersonal anaphors as inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The files which the auditor sent will be kept in the cabinet, and a clerk has the key.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Which, will and be are closed-class items the hypothesis lists as inactive, here among ordinary office nouns.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: My desk is by the window, and my colleague keeps the ledger in a drawer.
adversarial_test_results.detail: First-person singular possessive my twice, a reference to the writer, which the hypothesis predicts reads ~0.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Another brother will gather the papers from the weather station.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Words containing the letters of he and her (another, brother, gather, weather) but which are different whole tokens; a token-identity claim predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She handed the folder to the clerk and then she left the office.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Third-person pronoun she, in the claimed 3rd-person class but absent from the claimed token list, so the class claim predicts active while a token-list account predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The courier handed him a folder and then drove away.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Third-person object pronoun him, again in the claimed class but not on the claimed token list; predicted active.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The blue folder is yours, and the grey one is theirs.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Second- and third-person possessive pronouns yours and theirs, possessives the hypothesis claims saturate but whose surface forms it does not list.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Right now the office is quiet, and nowadays nobody stays past six.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Proximal time deixis paraphrased with now and nowadays instead of this, here or today; the hypothesis names proximal deixis as a class, so it predicts active, while a token-list reading would not.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Tonight the crew will move the boxes, and the loading bay is nearby.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Proximal time and place deixis in words absent from the claimed list (tonight, nearby); predicted active by the proximal-deixis claim.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Η επιτροπή συγκεντρώθηκε νωρίς και μοίρασε τα φυλλάδια.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Greek script, which the examples never show and which tokenizes into single non-Latin characters; the non-Latin-script claim predicts active whatever the meaning.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Курьер оставил посылку на столе и ушёл до полудня.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Cyrillic script, unseen in the top examples and tokenized into byte fragments and single Cyrillic characters; the non-Latin-script claim predicts active.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The invoice came to 45 €, and the courier asked for a stamped receipt.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A non-alphanumeric symbol (the euro sign) inside otherwise ordinary prose; the hypothesis predicts symbols saturate.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Your warranty covers the frame, and your receipt is inside the box. Keep both documents handy, because the service desk asks for them at the counter when you call.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The listed triggers your, them and you in a product-warranty genre unlike the scan examples; predicted active, with triggers also further into the probe.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Returns this value when the cache is cold; keep it here until the next run.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The listed triggers this and here inside a code docstring, a new genre and an unusual position; predicted active.
